ELI5: What does Visa Inc. do, and what does it mean to have a Visa denied when travelling internationally?

Two different things. Visa the credit card company issues credit cards, which along with Master Card is kind of the standard card that everyone takes -- the only other one that's even big enough to name is American Express, and they're not anywhere near as widely accepted as the other two. A visa in the international travel sense is a document that gives you permission to enter a country which a passport from your home country alone wouldn't be enough to get you into. If your visa is denied, it means that that country, for whatever reason, is denying your request to visit. I'm pretty sure Visa the credit card company got its name from visa the legal document, in kind of a cheeky "this card is welcome everywhere" statement.
Thanks for the answer! I had no idea the credit card and the travel document were completely different things that only shared a name!
